## Taxable income from Luka's 2025 backdoor Roth conversion: $6,748

**Answer: $6,748 of the $7,000 conversion is taxable income for 2025 (Form 8606 line 18). Only $252 comes out tax-free. The other $6,748 of after-tax basis carries forward to 2026 (line 14).**

**Why:** The December 2024 plan assumed the conversion would be tax-free. But it left Luka's rollover IRA (SYN-12040002) in place, and that account held $187,544.92 of pre-tax money at 31 December 2025. Under the pro-rata rule, a conversion is never treated as coming only from the new nondeductible contribution. Form 8606 compares the $7,000 basis with all of Luka's traditional IRA money combined (year-end balance plus the amount converted).

| Form 8606 line | Figure |
|---|---|
| 1–3, 5: basis (2025 nondeductible contribution; prior basis $0) | $7,000.00 |
| 6: traditional IRAs at 12/31/2025 (rollover IRA $42,871.51 Larkspur Core Bond Fund + $142,362.18 Fernhollow Large Cap Index Fund + $2,311.23 cash; SYN-12040003 at $0) | $187,544.92 |
| 8: converted | $7,000.00 |
| 9: line 6 + line 8 | $194,544.92 |
| 10: line 5 ÷ line 9 (rounded to 3 places) | 0.036 |
| 11: nontaxable part | $252.00 |
| **18: taxable part** | **$6,748.00** |
| **14: basis carried to 2026** | **$6,748.00** |
